conbody.p: is a popular choice for podcast production because it is free, cross-platform, and capable of professional-quality results. This topic outlines a typical podcast production workflow.

ol.li: Test your microphone levels — aim for peaks around -12 dB to leave headroom
Record in a quiet room with minimal echo
Use a pop filter to reduce plosive sounds (p, b, t)
Set your project to 44,100 Hz, 32-bit float for editing flexibility
Record a few seconds of silence at the start for a noise profile
Use 's Record button or press R
Monitor levels in the recording meter — stay in the green zone
If you make a mistake, pause briefly and re-record the sentence (you will edit it out later)

section.title: Post-Production
section.p: After recording, process your audio in this order:

ol.li: Noise reduction — remove background noise using the noise profile from your silence recording
Editing — trim mistakes, long pauses, and false starts
— bring the peak level to -1.0 dB
— even out volume differences (threshold -18 dB, ratio 3:1)
Export — export as MP3 at 128 kbps mono for distribution

section.title: Getting Started with Podcasting
section.p: If you are new to podcasting, start simple: record, trim the beginning and end, and export as MP3. As you gain experience, explore noise reduction, compression, and other effects to polish your sound.
